name: Elioenai
overview: Elioenai was a male priest from the tribe of Levi, specifically a descendant of Aaron, serving in a unique role as a priest with a trumpet. His priestly duties are noted in Nehemiah 12:41, highlighting his participation in temple worship during the post-exilic period. This role underscores his importance in the Levitical priesthood and the musical aspect of worship in Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Elioenai means 'my eyes [look] to YHWH,' reflecting a devotion and focus on the Lord. This proper Hebrew name is recorded in Nehemiah 12:41 and does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries a meaningful expression of faith.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Elioenai as a descendant of Aaron, which establishes his Levitical priestly lineage. Beyond this connection, no additional family relationships are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Elioenai's significance lies in his role as a Levitical priest who contributed to the worship of God through music, specifically by playing the trumpet. His presence in Nehemiah 12:41 during the temple ceremonies reflects the restoration of proper worship practices after the exile. As a descendant of Aaron, he represents the continuation of the priestly line entrusted with maintaining God's covenant worship.
